paper.title: VeriAgent: A Tool-Integrated Multi-Agent System with Evolving Memory for PPA-Aware RTL Code Generation
paper.central_claim: VeriAgent: a PPA-aware tool-integrated multi-agent framework (Programmer, Correctness, PPA agents with EDA tools) plus an Evolved Memory Mechanism (Rule/Structure/EDA-Signal memory nodes managed by insert/refine/discard) that enables continual improvement without retraining; maintains functional correctness and gives large PPA gains on VerilogEval and RTLLM.

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref=null: claude-kimi worker run, no per-call receipt exposed to the worker; model type per template (haiku slot -> claude-sonnet-5-5[1m]).

missing_sections: Fig.1 overview and Fig.2 win-rate bars are images, absent from text (no page_images in manifest)

rationale: EDA工具闭环+三类进化记忆，报告PPA大幅提升；但记忆构建/评测流未分离、测试台可能入环、功耗等指标异常、无成本与方差，记忆因果证据弱。

evidence.quote: In this work, we propose a PPA-aware, tool-integrated multi-agent framework for high-quality verilog code generation.
evidence.support_explanation: Central system claim.

evidence.quote: A dedicated memory manager dynamically maintains the memory pool
evidence.support_explanation: Evolved Memory Mechanism: memory manager maintains a pool of structured nodes from execution trajectories.

evidence.quote: existing systems generally lack a long-term optimization memory mechanism
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap: no accumulation/refinement of optimization knowledge across design iterations.

evidence.quote: Each memory unit is represented as a structured memory node consisting of trigger conditions, guidance, and metadata.
evidence.support_explanation: Node schema: trigger, guidance, metadata (three types: Rule, Structure, EDA Signal).

evidence.quote: Specifically, the context description together with all candidate triggers are provided to the LLM, which acts as a semantic selector to identify the most relevant triggers and memory nodes.
evidence.support_explanation: Read path: LLM selects triggers over the whole candidate list; top-3 nodes are injected (Sec.3.1).

evidence.quote: Beyond memory activation during generation, the Memory Manager continuously evolves the memory pool after each task execution.
evidence.support_explanation: Write path runs after every task; the paper does not separate construction tasks from evaluated tasks.

evidence.quote: Otherwise, the candidate node is considered redundant and discarded.
evidence.support_explanation: Decide(insert/refine/discard) is an LLM judgement; there is no measured-utility admission, retirement, versioning or size bound.

evidence.quote: The Correctness Agent ensures functional validity by executing testbenches and analyzing simulation results.
evidence.support_explanation: Testbench simulation is inside the generation loop; whether it is the benchmark's scoring testbench is not stated.

evidence.quote: considered successfully solved if at least one candidate passes all provided testbenches
evidence.support_explanation: pass@k scored with 'provided testbenches' - the same artifact type used for in-loop feedback (our reading).

evidence.quote: The Programmer Agent interacts with the Correctness Agent and the PPA Agent for at most two rounds respectively.
evidence.support_explanation: At most two feedback rounds; memory top-3 by LLM matching in the same paragraph.

evidence.quote: we employ a smaller model (
evidence.support_explanation: Retrieval/triggering use a smaller model (GPT-4o-mini) to cut cost; no cost numbers given.

evidence.quote: as the backbone models and the sampling temperature is set to 0.8.
evidence.support_explanation: Sampled generation at T=0.8; one set of numbers reported, no seeds.

evidence.quote: The evaluation pipeline uses Yosys and OpenROAD through NanGate45 process technology simulations.
evidence.support_explanation: PPA flow: Yosys/OpenROAD/NanGate45 on RTLLM v2.0 following Chen et al. 2025.

evidence.quote: The benchmark includes 50 problems covering combinational and sequential circuits, arithmetic modules, and control logic.
evidence.support_explanation: RTLLM has 50 problems; Table 2 lists 44 designs (our count).

evidence.quote: The relative PPA score is obtained by normalizing each design with respect to the original reference implementation provided by the benchmark.
evidence.support_explanation: Stated definition; reported scores equal the ratio of column geometric means (Table 2) over different valid-design subsets (our recomputation: 44 original, 38 ChipSeek, 32 GPT-4o, 41 Gemini).

evidence.quote: N/A indicates no functionally correct and synthesizable design.
evidence.support_explanation: Failures are visible in Table 2: our count of N/A is 12 (VeriAgent gpt-4o), 3 (gemini3), 6 (ChipSeek-R1) of 44 rows.
Original div_16bit delay/area/power.
Same delay and area as the original but ~1,600x lower power; implausible for a structurally similar combinational divider, suggests a protocol difference between columns (our inference).
ChipSeek-R1 power stays at the original order of magnitude, unlike VeriAgent.
Original adder_8bit; VeriAgent shows 0.3 / 49.21 / 1.12e-06 (28x lower power at near-identical area).
Original geometric means.
Delay x1.15 and area x1.16 better but power x3.85 lower; the power term supplies most of the 5.1x score.
Gemini: delay x1.42, area x1.30, power x4.6 relative to original.
ChipSeek-R1 adder delays of 0.07 ns (vs original 0.84 ns) are implausible for a 16-bit adder, hinting that this column's numbers come from a different flow.

evidence.quote: Overall, VeriAgent achieves the best results on most individual metrics as well as the highest mean relative PPA score.
evidence.support_explanation: Headline: Relative PPA 1.000 (original), 2.196 (ChipSeek-R1), 5.119 (gpt-4o), 8.539 (gemini3).

evidence.quote: between two methods by comparing their PPA scores on tasks where both methods successfully produce synthesizable designs.
evidence.support_explanation: Win rate is conditioned on tasks where both succeeded; VeriPPA numbers copied from its paper under a different protocol.

evidence.quote: Since VeriOpt uses a different evaluation protocol and dataset from ours and does not release detailed implementation information, we compare the results of VeriPPA reported in its original paper for comparison.
evidence.support_explanation: Cross-protocol comparison to VeriPPA; VeriOpt not compared.

evidence.quote: The ablation variants are constructed progressively, where each configuration removes one additional component based on the previous variant.
evidence.support_explanation: Cumulative ablation: Full 5.119/8.539 -> w/o Memory 3.839/6.541 -> w/o Tool Feedback 3.344/5.189 -> w/o PPA Analyzer 2.724/3.405 (GPT-4o/Gemini).

evidence.quote: Removing the memory module leads to a noticeable performance drop, indicating that accumulated design experience plays an important role in guiding optimization.
evidence.support_explanation: Memory contribution is ~23-25% of the relative PPA score in this ablation.

evidence.quote: While an ideal system could rely on a manually curated memory bank designed by hardware experts
evidence.support_explanation: No comparison to a static/expert-curated memory or to a non-evolving memory.

evidence.quote: In contrast, our framework directly leverages modern closed-source foundation models and achieves very high correctness.
evidence.support_explanation: Functional comparison pits tool/testbench-feedback agent against training-based small models and direct prompting.

evidence.quote: Overall, these results suggest that functional correctness on current benchmarks is approaching saturation on existing benchmarks.
evidence.support_explanation: Authors concede saturation; Direct Gemini3 already 91.7/94.9 on VerilogEval-Human pass@1/10.

evidence.quote: successfully optimizes only a small subset of tasks, while our framework consistently produces valid implementations for a significantly larger portion of the benchmark.
evidence.support_explanation: Valid-implementation claim vs Table 2 N/A counts (12 for gpt-4o).

gap.author_gap: RTL generation ignores PPA, uses EDA feedback shallowly as one-shot signals, and has no long-term optimization memory (E003).

claims.text: VeriAgent maintains very high functional correctness on VerilogEval and RTLLM v1.1.
claims.setting: GPT-4o and Gemini-3-Pro-Preview, T=0.8, pass@1/5/10 and Syn@5/Func@5
claims.baseline_control: Training-based RTL models and Direct prompting of the same backbones
claims.selection_vs_test: Testbench simulation feedback inside the loop; pass@k scored with 'provided testbenches'
claims.result_denominator: Gemini: Human pass@1 91.7->98.1, Machine 88.8->97.9; GPT-4o RTLLM Func@5 72.4 (below ChipSeek-R1 82.8)
claims.allowed_conclusion: Feedback-equipped agents score higher than direct prompting on saturated benchmarks; attribution to the memory or to hidden-test feedback is not possible.

claims.text: VeriAgent delivers significant PPA improvements (Relative PPA 5.119 / 8.539 vs ChipSeek-R1 2.196).
claims.setting: RTLLM v2.0, Yosys + OpenROAD, NanGate45, 44 listed designs
claims.baseline_control: Original benchmark designs and ChipSeek-R1 (flow identity unverified)
claims.selection_vs_test: Memory evolves on the same benchmark
claims.result_denominator: Valid designs 44 / 38 / 32 / 41 for original / ChipSeek-R1 / gpt-4o / gemini3
claims.allowed_conclusion: Under the authors' tables, VeriAgent's mean power-weighted PPA ratio is higher than ChipSeek-R1's; magnitude and attribution are unreliable until the power/delay measurements are explained.

claims.text: Evolved memory contributes to improvement without retraining.
claims.baseline_control: w/o Memory (same rounds and base LLM)
claims.allowed_conclusion: Disabling the memory manager lowers the reported score by ~23-25% in one run each; retained, transferable improvement is not shown.

claims.text: VeriAgent beats VeriPPA and ChipSeek-R1 in pairwise win rate on overlapping tasks.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Not checkable from text; cross-protocol and conditional on both-success.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: In the authors' own tables, the tool-in-the-loop agents with memory report higher functional and PPA scores than the original designs and than their disabled-memory variant; whether memory builds retained gains on unseen tasks, and whether PPA numbers are comparable across columns, is unresolved.
assessment.unresolved: Memory construction vs evaluation streams; hidden-test feedback; power/delay anomalies and aggregation over unequal subsets; flow identity for ChipSeek-R1/VeriPPA; cost; seeds; prompts and node examples; Fig.2 contents.

G.reason: Real, specific gap (PPA ignored, shallow tool feedback, no accumulation) with relevant neighbours named, but the memory-as-gap is a transplant of generic agent memory and neighbours (ChipSeek-R1, VeriPPA, VeriOpt) are only cited, not studied.

M.reason: Tool-in-the-loop plus trigger-guidance memory is a coherent mechanism, but no mechanism-level account or node examples show why memory should raise PPA, and the retention decision is an unexamined LLM call.

X.reason: Node schema, read path and insert/refine/discard are described, but prompts, K, thresholds, initial memory, memory size and order are absent; no gate, versioning or retirement; testbench role unclear.

E.measurement.reason: Standard tools (Yosys/OpenROAD) but unexplained 10^3x power drops at unchanged delay/area, implausible ChipSeek-R1 delays, a headline ratio of per-column geometric means over unequal valid subsets (12 N/A in one column), and VeriPPA compared across protocols.

E.causality.reason: A w/o-Memory toggle exists on two backbones, but the ablation is cumulative and single-run, there is no static/expert memory, no unified-baseline PPA comparison, and the PPA Agent/tool feedback explains more of the score than memory.

E.holdout.reason: No separation of memory-construction tasks from reported tasks, no initial-memory or order disclosure, and in-loop testbench identity unstated, after reading Sec.2.3, 3.1 and 3.3 (no appendix).
search_scope: Sec.5 conclusion; paper has no appendix

E.statistics.reason: Benchmark sizes and N/A failures are visible; no seeds, variance, CI or tests despite T=0.8 sampling.

E.cost.reason: No LLM-call, token, wall-clock or synthesis-time numbers for agents, memory manager or EDA runs; only a remark that a smaller model handles retrieval.
